name: Abarta

attributes.attribute: tricked the Fianna onto his horse and held them in the Otherworld
freed the Fianna and refused Abarta membership

sources: Joyce, Patrick Weston. Ancient Celtic Romances. London: Parkgate Books, 1997, 223+.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Abarta is a minor god of the Fomorians, an ancient and monstrous race. He appears in tales of the Fianna, the hero band, and hoped to join that elite. He came to them as a lazy man seeking work. Fionn Mac Cumhaill led the Fianna. He took Abarta into service and named him Gialla Deacair, the lazy servant. Abarta tricked the men onto his frail old horse. The horse carried them to the Otherworld. Abarta held them captive there. After many magical battles Fionn freed them. After that crime Fionn refused Abarta a place in the band.

okr.objective: Describe Abarta as a Fomorian trickster of the Fianna cycle.
